verdict.rationale: x402 documents an agent-driven pay-and-retry flow: the server quotes a price, the agent signs a payment from an agentic wallet, and the facilitator settles and returns the resource with confirmation. That covers a payment credential and a confirmed transaction. However, x402 is explicitly designed for per-request payments "without checkout pages", and merchant checkout sessions appear only as a single integration line ("agents can authorize payment sessions directly"). Missing for 10: documented checkout-session lifecycle and order-confirmation semantics for merchant purchases, a scoped/delegated payment credential beyond a funded agent wallet, and hands-on evidence of a full end-to-end merchant checkout.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can complete a purchase end-to-end — checkout session, delegated payment credential, confirmed order

citations.quote: x402-enable a merchant checkout built on Payment Acceptance so agents can authorize payment sessions directly.
The client signs a payment and sends the request again with proof of payment attached
Agentic accounts let an AI agent hold funds and act through a Coinbase account or wallet. For an x402 buyer, the account is the source of USDC that the agent uses to pay for a service.
Escrow is explicit, limits are cryptographically signed, and buyers retain defined refund and withdrawal semantics.
